Then the whole mess of constant stuttering, awful pop up and overall poor performances started. And, to put a cherry on top of all that, they also removed all songs from the Russian radio station due to expired licenses and you have to manually mod 'em back in. GTA IV is the absolute best game in the series. Its dark atmosphere, deep characters, and gritty story are on another level. The open world pulls you right in it's a bleak, realistic city, and you're just an immigrant trying to survive and escape your past.

I remember playing GTA IV for hundreds of hours when I was a kid/teenager. But now I understand that I couldn't have possibly appreciated the game for what it was. See, English is not my mother tounge. And, like every other GTA game, the fourth installment is filled to the brim with funny and satirical bits and gags that sometimes appear in the middle of a serious conversation between the characters. Even though the "maturity" of the jokes is ussualy between fifth and ninth grade, when they catch you off guard with their bluntness, the gigling is unavoidable(example below).

Every GTA game relies heavily on voices, accents, radio. This game is no exeption. Amazing voice acting, plethora of funny and sometimes indigestible accents, large collection of radio stations, great cutscenes.

The game now has Steam achievements for both the base game and two DLCs.

Joke example(not really a spoiler):
The characters are talking about killing the guy who owes them money and whatnot. Niko should find him through the dating website. And suddenly we find out that the internet cafe Niko should go to is called TW@.

Got the game on sale for 30% of its price. Having a blast!

After 40 hours, GTA IV was uninstalled, never to return. The first 20 hours or so were delirium, the other 20 an increasingly dull grind. The gameplay is very monotonous and key elements are simply put clunky. Given the emphasis on gunfights, the poor execution is disappointing. Nico actually drops his gun when running out of ammo, so I have to buy him a new one, it is more luck than skill when I win etc. Nico is always on the lookout for more money but practically the only thing he can buy are clothes! Then there is the infamous cell phone, and the in-game friends that call to invite Nico into tedious activities, and so on and so on.

The story is uncontrolled and episodic and the various underworld types are more broad caricatures than actual people. The game perhaps wants to criticize US capitalism and crime but the scenes completely undermine all serious commentary. The most absurd example is a broad daylight bank robbery in the metropolitan area. It is utterly ludicrous for three criminals to shoot and outshoot police, escape with the money and then return to status quo -- with zero repercussions!

Good game with interesting characters and I like the style and setting of Liberty City. But be warned, the vanilla port of this game is genuinely bad. Using FusionFIX is a must in order to enjoy this game.

This game also gets repetitive, as most missions involve driving from "Point A" to "Point B," taking out a guy for money, then talking to another guy who needs someone else eliminated. Rinse and repeat. Even GTA V and San Andreas had more mission variety than this game. I still enjoyed it this way, but I can understand if people do get bored of this. After all, most of us in our childhood only played GTA for the free-roam.

Speaking of free-roam, I really enjoyed the side activities of this game, hanging out with your friends and cousin never got old. Oh yeah you could also go on dates with certain girls on Lovemeet.net ;D

Overall, still an amazing game for it's open-world, writing and memorable characters.

My first time playing a GTA game from start to finish. It plays really slowly and awkwardly, so the combat or driving isn't very exciting which is 90% of the game. The other 10% is optional mini-games you can do to make your friends like you more, which can get old depending on how frequently you do them (and also gets frustrating when someone is annoyed you haven't hung out with them in a while). There's also virtually zero music throughout the entire game except for radio songs and a couple of scenes.

However, I really liked a lot of the dialogue writing. Some really good laughs that got me, and it was nice seeing characters start off as one-dimensional nothing burgers receive more complex emotional depth (or a dramatic send-off) as the story went on. I wouldn't want to replay it any time soon, but am really interested to watch or read about anything else the game had to offer that I missed. Sucks that you require several mods just to get it working properly though.

Grand Theft Auto IV is a very fun game. Although i have seen better graphics before in does not change the fact that it is one of my favourite games. The story is very interesting: you are a russian who comes to america on a boat because your cousin tells you that he is rich and has nice cars, a mansion and hot girls but when you finally get to his house you are not happy with what you see. that is only a very vague idea of the actual story. the gameplay is very fun and i would highly recommend it to anyone.

You are a contract killer, you are a bank robber, you are a narcotics traficker, you are a hero, you are a villian. All of these things you do not want to do but there is one sence of motivation and that is locate and murder the man who betrayed you and your friends as boys , killing everyone leaving you the only survivor from the villiage during the war. Arriving to Liberty City in the early 2000's you are fresh off the boat, an illegal immigrant, dressed in track pants, boots, jacket and sometimes ski mask.

Game has serious story flaws in the begining due a speculation of cut BETA content and feels a bit rushed/out of place; although it does pick up around a quarter of the way in you will not be able to put this game down. Seriously amazing story arch and perfect additional content being Episodes from Liberty City. Highly recommended.

reason.text: Negative reviews from this period mostly object to Take-Two's legal action against the OpenIV modding tool, which a news headline from the same month also covers.
Other negative reviews focus on forced launcher and account linking, the removal of Games for Windows Live, and poor optimization.
